context.title: The Kingdom Tears Apart
context.summary: Rehoboam rejects the elders' advice and threatens heavier burdens, so the ten northern tribes make Jeroboam king. Jeroboam sets up golden calves at Bethel and Dan.
context.background: Shechem, where the meeting happens, was an old covenant site in the north (Joshua 24). Bethel and Dan sat at the southern and northern edges of Jeroboam's kingdom, giving his people alternatives to Jerusalem. His festival in the eighth month imitated the Feast of Tabernacles held in the seventh.

customs.note: Probably a cruel kind of barbed whip, worse than an ordinary lash.
An old rallying cry to leave the assembly — here a declaration of independence (compare 2 Samuel 20:1).

watchFor: The elders urge Rehoboam to be a servant to the people (v. 7).
Jeroboam's words about the calves echo Aaron's at Sinai (v. 28).

people.name: Rehoboam
people.summary: He enlarges the people, the successor of Solomon on the throne, and apparently his only son. He was the son of Naamah “the Ammonitess,” some well-known Ammonitish princess (1 Kings 14:21; 2 Chr. 12:13).

people.name: Solomon
people.summary: Peaceful, (Heb. Shelomoh), David’s second son by Bathsheba, i.e., the first after their legal marriage (2 Sam. 12). He was probably born about B.C. 1035 (1 Chr. 22:5; 29:1).

people.name: Jeroboam
people.summary: The son of Nebat (1 Kings 11:26-39), “an Ephrathite,” the first king of the ten tribes, over whom he reigned twenty-two years (B.C. 976-945).

people.name: Nebat
people.summary: Sight; aspect, the father of Jeroboam, the king of Israel (1 Kings 11:26, etc.).

people.name: Ahijah
people.summary: A prophet of Shiloh (1 Kings 11:29; 14:2), called the “Shilonite,” in the days of Rehoboam. We have on record two of his remarkable prophecies, 1 Kings 11:31-39, announcing the rending of the ten tribes from Solomon; and 1 Kings 14:6-16, delivered to Jeroboam’s wife, foretelling the death of Abijah the king’s son, the destruction of Jeroboam’s house, and the captivity of Israel “beyond the river.”

people.name: David
people.summary: Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life. His mother’s name is not recorded.

people.name: Jesse
people.summary: Firm, or a gift, a son of Obed, the son of Boaz and Ruth (Ruth 4:17, 22; Matt. 1:5, 6; Luke 3:32). He was the father of eight sons, the youngest of whom was David (1 Sam. 17:12).

people.name: Israel
people.summary: One who follows on another’s heels; supplanter, (Gen. 25:26; 27:36; Hos. 12:2-4), the second born of the twin sons of Isaac by Rebekah. He was born probably at Lahai-roi, when his father was fifty-nine and Abraham one hundred and fifty-nine years old.

people.name: Judah
people.summary: Praise, the fourth son of Jacob by Leah.

people.name: Adoniram
people.summary: One who was “over the tribute;” i.e., “over the levy.” He was stoned by the Israelites after they had revolted from Rehoboam (2 Chr. 10:18).

people.name: Benjamin
people.summary: The younger son of Jacob by Rachel (Gen. 35:18). His birth took place at Ephrath, on the road between Bethel and Bethlehem, at a short distance from the latter place.

people.name: Shemaiah
people.summary: A prophet in the reign of Rehoboam (1 Kings 12:22-24).

people.name: Ephraim
people.summary: Double fruitfulness (“for God had made him fruitful in the land of his affliction”). The second son of Joseph, born in Egypt (Gen. 41:52; 46:20).

people.name: Dan
people.summary: The fifth son of Jacob. His mother was Bilhah, Rachel’s maid (Gen. 30:6, “God hath judged me”, Heb. dananni).

people.name: Levi
people.summary: The third son of Jacob by Leah. The origin of the name is found in Leah’s words (Gen. 29:34), “This time will my husband be joined [Heb. yillaveh] unto me.”

places.name: Shechem
places.summary: A city in Samaria (Gen. 33:18), called also Sichem (12:6), Sychem (Acts 7:16). It stood in the narrow sheltered valley between Ebal on the north and Gerizim on the south, these mountains at their base being only some 500 yards apart.

places.name: Egypt
places.summary: The land of the Nile and the pyramids, the oldest kingdom of which we have any record, holds a place of great significance in Scripture.

places.name: Judah (Southern)
places.summary: Added from Digital Manna places-1257 (LPF sync 2026-10-13)

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

places.name: Israel
places.summary: Kingdom, -974 to -720 (2Chr.10.19 to 2Kgs.17.6); added from Digital Manna places-1256 (LPF sync 2026-10-13)

places.name: Penuel
places.summary: Face of God, a place not far from Succoth, on the east of the Jordan and north of the river Jabbok. It is also called “Peniel.” Here Jacob wrestled (Gen. 32:24-32) “with a man” (“the angel”, Hos. 12:4.

places.name: Bethel
places.summary: A place in Central Palestine, about 10 miles north of Jerusalem, at the head of the pass of Michmash and Ai. It was originally the royal Canaanite city of Luz (Gen. 28:19).

places.name: Dan
places.summary: The fifth son of Jacob. His mother was Bilhah, Rachel’s maid (Gen. 30:6, “God hath judged me”, Heb. dananni).

events.title: Reign of Rehoboam
events.summary: Passage: 1 Kings 12:17–24. People: Rehoboam. Place: Jerusalem. Lasted about 17 years.

events.title: Reign of Jeroboam I
events.summary: Passage: 1 Kings 12:20–14:20. People: Jeroboam. Place: Samaria. Lasted about 22 years.
